title: Stories
coreMove: Embed the lesson in a sequence of choice and consequence so it can be retold without losing its action cue.
sourcePressure: The source is narrower here: stories carry lessons and practical meaning when the lesson is embedded in narrative, with challenge, connection, and creativity plots as supported labels.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating any anecdote as useful simply because it is a story.

sourceAnchors.name: challenge, connection, and creativity plots
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar says challenge, connection, and creativity plots appear in the books story taxonomy
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Challenge, connection, and creativity plots give story power three different engines instead of one vague praise of narrative.

sourceAnchors.name: embedded narrative lesson
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar says a story works best when the message is embedded in the narrative rather than stapled onto it
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The lesson should live in what happens, not in a label pasted after the last sentence.

hook: a story travels after you leave repeated literally
plot carries the lesson as generic opener
counterintuition: stories are not entertainment repeated without a test
tryThisNow: tell a story about your idea
add a beginning middle and end
examples: values poster replaced by team legend

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: a rescue trainer teaching new volunteers probe-line spacing
exampleSpecs.stakes: a search pattern fails if the rule stays a number
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Emily tells the story of one search where a skipped arm length changed the outcome, with the spacing lesson embedded in the sequence of moves
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Snow squeaks under the probe tips in the training field

exampleSpecs.audience: a head baker teaching patience to new apprentices
exampleSpecs.stakes: rushed fermentation ruins a weekend batch
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Nicolas builds the patience rule into the story of two loaves, one cut by the clock and one cut by the doughs signs
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 3:18 a.m., Nicolas taps two proofing baskets dusted with rice flour

exampleSpecs.audience: a nurse educator teaching calm escalation to new staff
exampleSpecs.stakes: tiny changes get missed if the protocol is just recited
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "Listen to what her mother noticed first," Frida says, then tells a handoff story where family observation and nurse action fit together
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Listen to what her mother noticed first," Frida says beside the isolette

exampleSpecs.audience: a mechanic teaching apprentices to diagnose recurring brake failures
exampleSpecs.stakes: bad repairs return to the street as safety risks
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Ben reconstructs one returned bike from first squeak to final test ride so the diagnostic rule is recoverable from the sequence
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Rain ticks on the repair-bay skylight while one orange bike hangs from the stand

exampleSpecs.audience: an organizer teaching new volunteers how trust builds
exampleSpecs.stakes: volunteers lose tenants if they lead with demands before listening
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Tomas chooses a connection plot where a quiet hallway conversation changes the order of action, and the lesson is never stated as a moral at the end
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Tomas one failed door-knocking night to notice who the tenants already trusted

exampleSpecs.audience: a professor teaching creativity under material limits
exampleSpecs.stakes: students treat constraints as unfair unless the plot shows breakthrough through limits
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Adaeze tell a redesign story where the missing material forces the student to invent a better hinge, embedding the creativity lesson in the turn
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You can hear the prototype hinge click wrong from across the lab

skillTargets: choose a story shape that matches the lesson
distinguish embedded lessons from pasted-on morals
diagnose when retelling mutates the intended meaning
design a sequence that carries an action cue

tryThisNowSpec: Take one rule you keep explaining and write the three beats of a true or fictional scene where a choice, a turn, and a consequence teach it without a pasted-on moral.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
